newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: S.LANKA SAYS NOT SUBSIDISING WHEAT FLOUR ANYMORE.
newsitem.headline: S.LANKA SAYS NOT SUBSIDISING WHEAT FLOUR ANYMORE.

text.p: Sri Lanka said on Thursday the government subsidy on wheat flour imports had been effectively removed after a retail price hike earlier this week.

"The government spent around 750 million rupees annually subsidising wheat flour imports. This figure had accumulated to two billion rupees," said P.B. Jaysurndera, a senior official of the finance ministry.
"By raising the price of wheat flour, we are virtually not subsidising it any more," Jayasundera told a news conference.
The Food Commissioner's Department on Monday raised the price of a kilogram of wheat flour by two rupees to 18.95 rupees, and that of a loaf of bread by 75 cents to 8.25 rupees.
The previous price hike was in August last year when the price of wheat flour was increased by three rupees and of bread by one rupee.
Sri Lanka's wheat imports fell by 14 percent to 913,000 tonnes last year from just over a million tonnes in 1995, the Central bank has said.

The government has said the island must prepare for a cut in state subsidies on food to fund the separatist war against the Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE), who are seeking an independent homeland in the north and east of Sri Lanka.
The government has allocated 44 billion rupees for defence this year, 22 percent of total government spending. ($1=58.8 rupees)
